title: Effective cartesian realization of a small-etale line module
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Every small-etale line module $L$ on $X$ admits an etale line presentation $P$ [def-trf-cartesian-line-presentation] whose specified small-etale module is exactly $L$. No uniqueness or morphism assertion is made.

source.place: Tags 03G7 and 03M3; descent.tex Tags 03DX, 03LC, 023T and 05VG. The atlas argument and its morphism argument are specialized to rank one.

proof.text: Restrict L to the small-etale site of an atlas scheme. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison] to its local rank-one frames. This gives an ordinary invertible module on the atlas. On its double overlap, full faithfulness lifts the canonical identification of the two restrictions to a transition isomorphism. Faithfulness proves the cocycle on triple overlaps.

For each scheme test W, the base change of the atlas is a scheme [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its projection is etale and surjective. Pull back the atlas module and its transition isomorphism. Effective fpqc descent [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] gives a module with an identification of this specified descent datum. The same theorem reflects local freeness of rank one, so the descended module is invertible. Apply the theorem to the etale covering sieve; it is fpqc by the inclusion of the fppf topology in the fpqc topology.

For every test map, both the tensor pullback of the module on the target and the module on the source realize the same pulled-back descent datum. Full faithfulness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] supplies their unique isomorphism preserving the atlas identifications. The identity and composition equations follow because their two sides induce the same atlas map. On small-etale tests, the atlas identifications give local additive section equivalences to L, agreeing on overlaps. Glue by the sheaf equalizer. Equality after the atlas cover proves scalar linearity and naturality. This is the required presentation; its line field is L by construction. Empty tests obey the same equalizer and descent argument.
